signin.title: What’ll it be?
signin.lead: Use the passkey on this device, or your username and password.
signin.passwordSet: Password saved. Sign in with it.

errors.invalidToken: That link is no longer valid. Ask the printer owner for a fresh one.
errors.tokenExpired: That link expired. Ask the printer owner for another.
errors.suspended: That account has been suspended. Ask whoever owns the printer.
errors.other: That sign-in attempt did not go through.

form.refused: That username and password do not match. Try again.
form.tooManyAttempts: Too many attempts. Wait a minute and try again.
form.passkeyRefused: That passkey was not accepted. Use your password instead.
form.inviteOnly: Pretty Please Print is invite-only — there is no sign-up. If you have not been invited yet, or you have forgotten your password, ask whoever owns the printer.

nudge.title: Tired of typing your password?
nudge.body: Save a passkey and this device signs you in with a fingerprint — nothing to remember, nothing to phish.

themes.glass: Glass — see-through panels over a colourful room
themes.auto: Follow the system — the diner by day, after hours in dark mode

slicer.help: Opens {slicer} on this machine. Needs the one-time helper — see the setup. Nothing happens if it is not installed — the download beside this works anywhere.

preferences.title: How you like it
preferences.lead: Your language, how the place looks, and the slicer named on the button of every ticket. Left to the house, each one follows the printer owner’s choice — today and when it changes.
preferences.languageHelp: Left to the house, your browser’s language comes first, if this app speaks it.
preferences.slicerHelp: Only the button’s name changes. The helper on your own machine decides which slicer opens.
preferences.refused: That is not on the menu. Pick from the list.

settingsDefaults.title: For everyone who has not chosen
settingsDefaults.lead: Each person can pick their own on their page; these are what everyone else gets, the sign-in page included.
settingsDefaults.languageHelp: For a browser that asks for no language this app speaks, or for none. A browser asking for English or French still gets it.
settingsDefaults.slicerHelp: The name on the slicer button of every ticket — “Open in your slicer” for another slicer. Only the label: the helper on each machine decides what opens.

setup.title: Before the doors open
setup.lead: Six short steps to get the counter ready. Each one can be skipped, and everything here can be changed later at Settings.
setup.leadAgain: The six steps a new instance starts with, to go through again. Everything here is also at Settings.
setup.reauthNote: Saving asks for your password or passkey again if you signed in more than five minutes ago, as it does at Settings.
setup.skipAll: Skip the rest of the setup
setup.skipAllHelp: It will not open by itself again. It stays at Settings, whenever you want it.
setup.doneAlready: This instance is past its first run; nothing here opens by itself any more.

toast.saved: Saved — in effect from the next request

account.lead: Your account is open: the link from the logs gave it a username and a password, and that is the way in that always works.
account.name: Name
account.hasPasskey: {count, plural, one {This account has a passkey. Signing in is a fingerprint or a face.} other {This account has # passkeys. Signing in is a fingerprint or a face.}}
account.passkeyWhy: One thing worth thirty seconds: save a passkey. It puts your fingerprint, face or device PIN where the password goes — nothing to remember, nothing to phish.
account.passkeyLater: Needs a browser that does passkeys, with JavaScript on. Not now? The account menu offers it whenever you like.

address.lead: Sign-in cookies, passkeys and every link in an e-mail are tied to one address: APP_URL, in .env.docker. This step only checks it — it stays in the environment.
address.match: They match: this is the address the app expects.
address.mismatch: They differ. Sign-in cookies are set for {app}, Better Auth refuses forms sent from anywhere else, and invitations and reset links point there — so from {seen}, signing in and passkeys fail, and links lead elsewhere. Open the app at {app}, or set APP_URL to the address people will use and restart the stack.
address.rpIdOk: Passkeys are bound to {rpId}, which covers {host}.
address.rpIdBad: Passkeys are bound to {rpId}, which does not cover {host}: browsers will refuse to make or use one. PASSKEY_RP_ID has to be {host} or a domain above it — and it is permanent once somebody has a passkey, so fix it before.

look.lead: For everyone who has not chosen on their own page, the sign-in page included. The same two defaults as at Settings, saved the same way.

mail.lead: Mail only ever delivers a link — an invitation, or a password reset. Without it the app shows you the link to hand over yourself, which works too.
mail.sendHelp: To your own address only, and at most {count} in {minutes} minutes.
mail.noneHow: To send mail, set one of SMTP_URL or RESEND_API_KEY in .env.docker, with MAIL_FROM for the address it comes from, then restart the stack:
mail.noneFine: Or leave it: running without mail is a supported way to run this app.

problem.noTransport: There is no transport to send through.
problem.tooMany: That makes {count} test messages in {minutes} minutes. Give it a moment before the next.
problem.refused: The transport refused the message. The app’s log says why.
problem.refusedCode: The transport refused the message ({code}). The app’s log says why.

slicer.lead: Every ticket has a button that opens its model in a slicer, through a small helper installed once on the computer with the printer. The button’s name first, then the helper.
slicer.platform: This browser says it runs on {os}.

os.other: a system the helper has no installer for

slicer.windowsNote: No administrator rights: it installs under your own profile, and -ExecutionPolicy Bypass applies to this one run only.

people.lead: Nobody gets in without an invitation. Send the first one from the guest list: by mail if mail is set up, or as a link you hand over yourself.
people.finish: Finish — take me to the pass
people.finishInvite: Finish and send the first invitation

revisit.title: First-run setup
revisit.body: The six steps a new instance starts with: the address, mail, the slicer helper and the rest.

passkey.done: Passkey saved. Next time, signing in is a fingerprint or a face — the password still works if you would rather.
passkey.failed: That did not complete. The account menu offers it again whenever you like.
